section.title: Ways in
section.intro: There is more than one door. The CAO is the one everybody points at, which is not the same as it being the best one for you. Some of these pay you. Some cost almost nothing. One of them is still open when you are thirty-four.

items.title: Apprenticeships
items.subtitle: They pay you
items.summary: On a payroll from the first week. Four years later you have a qualification and no debt. Nobody says this out loud in fifth year.
items.body:
An apprenticeship is a job with training bolted onto it. You are an employee from day one. You get a wage, it goes up every year, and you split your time between working and a classroom. At the end you hold a qualification the State recognises.

The part your careers talk skipped: apprenticeships stopped being only trades some time ago. There are apprenticeships in software, insurance, accountancy, engineering and logistics. Some go to degree level. Nobody updated the slides.

blocks.heading: The hard part is not the exams
blocks.text: It is finding an employer. No central system, no points, no offers day. You have to get a company to say yes. Ringing local firms directly works more often than people expect, mostly because almost nobody does it. Knowing somebody helps, which is the entire reason this website exists.

blocks.heading: If nobody will take you yet
blocks.text: Do a PLC in the same field first. You come out with something to show and somebody willing to vouch for you. It is not a step backwards, whatever way people say it to you.

blocks.heading: There is no age limit
blocks.text: People start at seventeen and at thirty-four. If you get this decision wrong it is not permanent, which is more than can be said for most of what you will be told this year.

blocks.heading: Where it ends up
blocks.text: Supervision, contracting, inspection, teaching, your own company. A fair number of qualified tradespeople out-earn the graduates who felt sorry for them at eighteen.

myths.myth: Apprenticeships are for people who aren't academic.
myths.reality: The exams fail people every year. Different difficulty, not a smaller one.
Software, insurance, finance, accountancy, engineering, logistics. Read the list before you decide what you are.

myths.myth: You'll earn less in the end.
myths.reality: You start four years earlier owing nothing. Do the sums yourself before you take anyone's word for it.

items.title: PLC and further education
items.subtitle: No points. Barely any fees.
items.summary: A year or two, no points requirement, and you apply straight to the college. Leads to work, or to the same degree by a quieter road.
items.body:
A Post Leaving Certificate course is a full-time, practical course run by an Education and Training Board or a further education college. You apply directly. There is no points requirement and there is no race.

People call it a fallback. They say it the way you would describe a spare tyre. It leads directly into work in plenty of fields, and it is one of the surest ways into a degree for anyone whose Leaving Certificate went sideways.

blocks.heading: It goes somewhere
blocks.text: Finish a PLC and there are arrangements that take you into higher education from there. For some courses it is a more reliable way into the same degree than competing on points at eighteen. Ask the college which courses their students actually progress to, and ask for numbers.

blocks.heading: The deadline has probably not passed
blocks.text: No central system means no single closing date. Plenty of colleges take applications deep into the summer, including after results come out. This is the door that is still open on the day you decide everything has gone wrong.

blocks.heading: The format is different
blocks.text: Smaller classes, continuous assessment, work you do with your hands as often as your memory. If the Leaving Certificate never suited you, that may have been the format rather than you.

blocks.heading: It also opens the apprenticeship door
blocks.text: A year of relevant training makes an employer a lot more likely to take you on. You stop being a stranger with no experience.

myths.myth: It's what you do if you fail.
myths.reality: It's what a lot of people do who arrive at the same degree by a different road, and some who wanted the qualification itself all along.
QQI awards are recognised nationally, and in a good many fields the practical training is exactly what they're looking for.

items.title: CAO and college
items.subtitle: The one you've already heard about
items.summary: Your school will cover the form. This is the part they tend to leave out: the points may not apply to you, you can start lower down, and none of it is final.
items.body:
The Central Applications Office handles almost every higher education course in the country. You rank courses, your results become points, offers come out in rounds in August. You know this already.

What gets left out is how much give there is inside the system.

blocks.heading: The points everyone quotes may not be your points
blocks.text: HEAR offers places on reduced points to students from socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds. There is a real chance you qualify, and it costs nothing to find out. It goes in with your CAO application and the deadline is earlier than the one on the poster. This is the most useful sentence on this website and most of the people it applies to never act on it.

blocks.heading: You can come in at a lower level
blocks.text: Level 6 and Level 7 courses take far fewer points than honours degrees, and many of them let you progress into the degree afterwards. Arriving a year later is still arriving.

blocks.heading: Nothing you write on that form at seventeen is binding
blocks.text: People transfer, repeat, drop out and come back, or turn up at twenty-three as mature students and get assessed on their life instead of their Leaving Certificate. Treating the CAO as a verdict on your character has ruined more years than any course choice on it.

blocks.heading: Money is the smaller problem
blocks.text: Between SUSI, the 1916 Bursary and the funds colleges keep quiet about, the cost gets reduced or covered for plenty of students. Settle the money question separately. Do not cross a course off because of a number you have not checked.

myths.myth: The points tell you how good the course is.
myths.reality: Points are demand. A high-points course is popular. That is all the number means.

myths.myth: I have to go now or never.
myths.reality: Mature entry exists at twenty-three exactly because plenty of people do not go now.

myths.myth: Missing my first choice means I've failed.
myths.reality: Most people miss their first choice. Then they get on with it and it turns out fine, which nobody tells you in August.

items.title: Studying in Europe
items.subtitle: Usually cheaper than staying home
items.summary: English-taught degrees across the continent at EU fee rates. A fraction of what the same thing costs in the UK, and sometimes less than Dublin.
items.body:
You are an Irish citizen, which makes you an EU student, which means you pay what a local pays anywhere in the union. In several countries that figure is small. Hundreds of degrees are taught entirely in English.

The Netherlands is the well-worn route. A large number of English-taught bachelor's degrees, an application system that expects foreigners, and student cities that are used to them. Germany and the Nordics teach in English too, at low or no tuition.

Almost nobody in an Irish school will raise this with you. It is not obscure and it is not difficult. It simply is not on the slides.

blocks.heading: Why this page is not about the UK
blocks.text: Fee arrangements for Irish students in the UK changed after Brexit and vary. Check the current position properly before you assume anything about it. The continent is the reliable value, which is why it is the one written up here.

blocks.heading: Entry works differently
blocks.text: Many European universities don't run a points race. Some admit anyone who meets a minimum standard, some use a lottery, some choose for themselves. A course that is unreachable on points here may not be unreachable there.

blocks.heading: Housing is the actual problem
blocks.text: Not fees. Beds. Student accommodation in Dutch cities is genuinely scarce and has to be sorted early. This is the thing that goes wrong for people, and it goes wrong in August.

blocks.heading: Check what Irish support follows you
blocks.text: Some Irish student supports apply to study elsewhere in the EU and some do not. Ask SUSI directly. Do not take the answer from a forum.

blocks.heading: What you get that isn't on the certificate
blocks.text: Living somewhere else at nineteen changes what you think is available to you, permanently. If you have not travelled much, that is the larger half of the value, and no prospectus will put a number on it.

myths.reality: Hundreds of degrees are taught in English, particularly in the Netherlands and the Nordics.
EU tuition is often below the Irish student contribution. Living costs are the variable, and not always upward.

myths.myth: An Irish employer won't take it seriously.
myths.reality: EU degrees are recognised across the EU. It is a normal qualification from a normal university.
